prompt: Which formula is the contrapositive of $P\to Q$?

answers.explanation: The contrapositive reverses the direction and negates both statements. It is equivalent to the original: if Q is false, P must also be false for the implication to hold.
Conjoining the statements neither reverses nor negates them.
This is the converse: it reverses direction but does not negate either statement.
The contrapositive is an implication; it does not assert that both statements are false.
This is the inverse: it negates both statements but keeps the original direction.
The premise needs to be not Q, not Q itself.
The conclusion needs to be not P, not P itself.
Negating the whole converse gives Q and not P; that is not contraposition.
This is false when both statements are true; the original and its contrapositive are true then.
A biconditional additionally requires the converse, which contraposition does not.
